Hi Hari / Emma — thanks for the details and the context.

Short answer: two pragmatic lanes that meet your constraints, with tradeoffs:

1) Seclusion (Customer-private VPC / on-prem package)
   - Fully customer-controlled network and KMS/HSM integration
   - No shared inference tenancy; logs and telemetry stay in your VPC/storage
   - Higher upfront engineering + infra lift (onboarding window ~4–8 weeks)
   - Recommended for customers with strict audit/airgap requirements or regulatory commitments

2) Reservation (Dedicated pool in Redwood-managed region, single-tenant)
   - Redwood manages runtime; dedicated GPUs reserved for your account only
   - We can surface customer-managed KMS, strict egress policies, and per-request audit trails
   - Faster onboarding (1–2 weeks) and lower operational lift for your team

Sizing (pilot baseline assumptions: 30k messages/month, average prompt 300 tokens, response 400 tokens, peak concurrency ~8):
- Seclusion (on-prem/VPC): start with 4xA40 / equivalent (or 8xA30) to hit p95 150–250ms on common gen models with local KV caching.
- Reservation (dedicated in Redwood): 2–4xA100S (or 4xA40) depending on model family; we recommend a 3-node reserved pool as the conservative starting point to ensure stable p95 under burst.

Ops notes: 1) If you want lowest unit cost with modest latency risk, Reservation + prefix caching is easiest. 2) For maximum compliance guarantees, Seclusion is the path but procurement/time-to-value is longer.

I attached a quick SOC2 snapshot and a draft sizing workbook (seclusion_vs_reservation_sizing.xlsx) — Marissa has a more detailed cost/throughput breakdown.

Next step proposal: 30-min call Wed to align on procurement path + sign MLP?

Thanks Tessa — adding some concrete numbers from our sizing runbook. Quoting your note below where helpful.

On Seclusion (customer-private):
- Baseline cluster: 4xA40 GPUs (or 8xA30) + 32 vCPU coordination nodes + 1TB NVMe caching layer
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~40–50k gen tokens/minute (depending on model family); p95: ~160–260ms with optimized kernels + local KV cache
- Onboarding: ~4–8 weeks including network/security review, KMS provisioning, and audit validation
- Cost ballpark (CSP-hosted VPC): infra + engineering runbook estimate = $XXk/month (we'll provide exact numbers in the workbook).

On Reservation (Redwood-managed dedicated pool):
- Baseline: 3 nodes of A100S-80GB (or equivalently 4xA40) to provide headroom for bursts and rolling upgrades
- Add burst lane: ability to spill to shared pool with strict routing rules (if allowed by MedVerity) — reduces committed spend but introduces co-location risk
- p95 target achievable at ~180–220ms with batching tuned for concurrency=8
- Onboarding: 1–2 weeks; we can ship IP allowlist + KMS integration in this window.

Deal-linked recommendations (RDW-6621):
- Pilot commitment: 3-month reservation for dedicated pool OR 3-month engagement to stage seclusion with milestone-based payments
- If MedVerity needs legal-level isolation, recommend parallel path: start on Reservation to hit time-to-value, run compliance workstream in parallel to migrate to Seclusion within 2–3 quarters.

Aditya — can you confirm whether we have a standard reserved SKU we can price for a 3-node pilot? Also any discount cadence for a 3-month reserved commitment vs 12-month?

Marissa
